Identities:
# Identities
## What the theme covers
Identities explores the nature of the self and what it is to be human. Recommended topics are lifestyles, health and well-being, beliefs and values, subcultures, and language and identity.

## Useful language
Describe yourself with ser for permanent traits (soy responsable) and estar for states (estoy cansado). Give opinions with en mi opinión, creo que and me parece que. Use gustar-type verbs: me encanta, me preocupa, me interesa. Talk about change with antes + imperfecto and ahora + presente: antes comía mal, pero ahora como sano.

## Ideas to discuss
Bilingualism and regional languages in Spain (catalán, euskera, gallego), indigenous languages in Latin America such as quechua and guaraní, and the influence of social media on self-image.

## Key terms
el estilo de vida: lifestyle, way of life
la salud: health, being healthy
el bienestar: well-being, welfare
los valores: values, principles
las creencias: beliefs, what people believe
pertenecer a: to belong to
la autoestima: self-esteem, self-worth
Experiences:
# Experiences
## What the theme covers
Experiences explores the events that shape our lives. Recommended topics are leisure activities, holidays and travel, life stories, rites of passage, customs and traditions, and migration.

## Useful language
Narrate the past with the pretérito indefinido for completed actions (fui a México) and the imperfecto for background and habits (cuando era niño, iba a la playa). Use the pluscuamperfecto for an earlier past: ya había visitado Madrid. Use the future and conditional for plans: el año que viene viajaré; si tuviera dinero, viajaría.

## Ideas to discuss
Festivals such as el Día de los Muertos, la Tomatina and las Fallas; la quinceañera as a rite of passage; migration from Latin America to the United States and Spain.

## Key terms
el ocio: leisure, free time
el viaje: the trip, the journey
las costumbres: customs, traditions
un rito de iniciación: a rite of passage
la migración: migration, moving country
los recuerdos: memories, souvenirs
Human ingenuity:
# Human ingenuity
## What the theme covers
Human ingenuity explores how human creativity and innovation affect our world. Recommended topics are entertainment, artistic expressions, communication and media, technology, and scientific innovation.

## Useful language
Weigh pros and cons with por un lado… por otro lado, la ventaja es que and la desventaja es que. Use the present subjunctive after expressions of doubt, emotion and necessity: es necesario que usemos la tecnología con cuidado; dudo que la inteligencia artificial resuelva todo. Use connectives such as sin embargo, no obstante, además and por lo tanto.

## Ideas to discuss
Social media and screen time, artificial intelligence, Spanish-language cinema and music, and the art of Frida Kahlo and Pablo Picasso.

## Key terms
las redes sociales: social media
la inteligencia artificial: artificial intelligence
el invento: the invention
los medios de comunicación: the media
el entretenimiento: entertainment, amusement
sin embargo: however, nevertheless
Social organization:
# Social organization
## What the theme covers
Social organization explores how groups of people organize themselves. Recommended topics are social relationships, community, social engagement, education, the working world, and law and order.

## Useful language
Use relative pronouns to build complex sentences: que, quien, donde, cuyo and lo que. Express obligation with tener que, deber and hay que. Make suggestions with se debería and sería mejor que + imperfect subjunctive. Use impersonal expressions such as es importante que + present subjunctive.

## Ideas to discuss
School systems in Spain and Latin America, volunteering (el voluntariado), youth unemployment, and protest movements such as the indignados in Spain.

## Key terms
la comunidad: the community
el voluntariado: volunteering, unpaid work
la educación: education, schooling
el desempleo: unemployment, being out of work
la huelga: a strike, industrial action
la ley: the law
Sharing the planet:
# Sharing the planet
## What the theme covers
Sharing the planet explores the challenges and opportunities faced by individuals and communities. Recommended topics are the environment, human rights, peace and conflict, equality, globalization, ethics, and urban and rural environment.

## Useful language
Persuade with hay que, es urgente que and debemos. Use the conditional with the imperfect subjunctive for hypotheses: si todos recicláramos, habría menos basura. Use the passive with se: se destruyen los bosques.

## Ideas to discuss
Deforestation in the Amazon, water shortages, inequality in Latin America, human rights and the memory of dictatorships, and urban life compared with rural life.

## Key terms
el medio ambiente: the environment
el calentamiento global: global warming
la basura: rubbish, waste
reciclar: to recycle
los derechos humanos: human rights
la desigualdad: inequality, being unequal
sostenible: sustainable, long-lasting
Paper 1: writing:
# Paper 1: writing
## The paper
Paper 1 is a writing paper. You choose one of three tasks and write a text of the type asked for: at SL 250–400 words in 1 hour 15 minutes, at HL 450–600 words in 1 hour 30 minutes. It is marked on language, message and conceptual understanding.

## Text types
Text types include the article, blog, email, letter, speech, diary entry, review, interview, brochure, report and proposal. Use the conventions of each type, such as a date, greeting and sign-off for a letter. Match the register to the audience: tú for friends and usted for formal writing. Formal letters open with Estimado/a señor/a and close with Atentamente.

## Tips
Plan purpose, audience and context first. Use a range of tenses including the subjunctive, connectives and idioms. Check accents, agreement and ser/estar.

## Key terms
el registro: register, the level of formality
el destinatario: the recipient, the audience
Estimado señor: formal letter greeting, Dear Sir
Atentamente: formal sign-off, Yours faithfully
Paper 2: listening and reading:
# Paper 2: listening and reading
## The paper
Paper 2 tests receptive skills. The listening section uses three audio texts; the reading section uses three written texts. Questions include multiple choice, true or false with justification, gap-filling, matching and short answers.

## Strategies
Read the questions before you listen or read. Look for synonyms and paraphrases rather than identical words. In true/false questions, the justification must be the words from the text. Watch for negatives such as no… nunca, ya no and tampoco, which change the meaning.

## Key terms
verdadero o falso: true or false
justifica: justify, give evidence
ya no: no longer, not any more
tampoco: neither, not either
Individual oral:
# Individual oral
## The assessment
The individual oral is the internal assessment. At SL you describe and discuss a visual stimulus linked to a theme; at HL you discuss an extract from one of the literary works you studied. It includes a presentation of up to 4 minutes, a follow-up discussion, and a general conversation on at least one other theme.

## How to do well
Link the stimulus to the theme and to the Spanish-speaking world. Use varied vocabulary and structures, and develop opinions. Use fillers such as bueno, pues and a ver naturally, and ask for clarification if needed: ¿podría repetir?

## Key terms
describir: to describe
en primer plano: in the foreground
al fondo: in the background
¿podría repetir?: could you repeat?
Literary works:
# Literary works
## Literature at HL
HL students study two literary works in Spanish. Literature helps you explore the themes in depth and builds vocabulary and cultural understanding. The HL individual oral discusses an extract from one of these works.

## Talking about literature
Discuss the plot (la trama), the characters (los personajes), the narrator (el narrador), the setting, the themes and the author's style. Use the present tense to describe events. Support points with short quotations and explain their effect. Popular works include La casa de Bernarda Alba by Lorca, Crónica de una muerte anunciada by García Márquez and short stories by Borges.

## Key terms
la trama: the plot
el personaje: the character
el narrador: the narrator
el fragmento: the extract
el tema: the theme
